<reason>CON built a sharp, sustained dilemma against PRO's core term: either "standing commitment" binds future resource allocation (in which case it forecloses reallocating scarce interceptors to a simultaneous Taiwan crisis, exactly what the resolution's own "even if it reduces resources for other priorities" clause invites us to weigh) or it doesn't bind anything beyond rhetoric (in which case PRO has covertly retreated to CON's conditional-renewal model under a different label). PRO's answers—distinguishing "revision" from "repeated rescue" and asserting a "continuing claim on resources" while individual transfers remain reallocable—were reasonable in spirit but never cleanly resolved which horn PRO was standing on, and CON's closing exploited that ambiguity effectively ("PRO never picks a horn"). PRO's predictability/deterrence mechanism was a decent affirmative case, but CON's rebuttal that two years of contested, periodically-renewed aid have neither produced the predicted Russian breakthrough nor produced concessions when aid was more assured was a solid grounded counter that PRO did not fully answer. Both sides handled the Pressure Questions format correctly (A1/A2 labels present), but CON's cross-examination exposed the load-bearing ambiguity in PRO's model more decisively than PRO's questions exposed anything comparably fatal in CON's. CON's Taiwan opportunity-cost point also landed harder given the resolution's explicit acceptance of tradeoffs, while PRO's "sequencing and reserves" response stayed abstract. Overall CON forced the more decisive, unresolved tension and kept the comparison cleaner through closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's pressure-question pincer (A3.1/A3.2, pressed home in A4.1-A4.2 and A5.1-A5.2) forcing PRO to choose between "standing" binding resources (foreclosing Taiwan reallocation) or not binding anything (collapsing into conditional renewal) was the decisive exchange; PRO's "continuing claim on resources" vs. "reallocable individual transfers" distinction in B4.3-B4.4 and B5.2 never fully closed that gap.</best_rebuttal>
